answer: Agents stake a bonded deposit per identity, and peers challenge any wallet suspected of splitting into clones. A challenger must post a matching bond and cite a unique proof-of-work nonce; if the accused is a sybil, its bond is slashed and paid to the challenger, so a sparrow cannot cheaply masquerade as a flock. Honest agents in the garden keep bonds small, while a canyon-sized farm of fake identities costs more than the rewards it could harvest, making mass duplication unprofitable.
